author: Pat Stout
title: Fed In A Box
text:
The financial markets are driven by interest rates . And the Federal Reserve plays a key role in setting the level of interest rates. Below I will explain why the Federal Reserve might be facing a Catch-22 and what an interest rate move might signal about economic growth.
President Trump has suggested via Tweets that he is unhappy with the Federal Reserve moving interest rates higher. The President feels that interest rates have moved higher too fast and that he prefers low interest rates. While I am in agreement with the President about the speed and magnitude of the interest rate hikes . My opinion or any other analyst that questions the moves by the Federal Reserve does not carry the weight of comments by the President.
The President’s comments place the Federal Reserve in a Catch-22. Should the Fed decide not to raise interest rates at the next meeting, then the question the market might ask is – did the President influence the independent Federal Reserve or do the Federal Reserve members see economic challenges ahead? If the market feels the Federal Reserve has lost its independence, then that would increase uncertainty. This could cause interest rates to increase as greater US Treasury issuance hits the market thanks to the tax cut. If the markets feel that the Federal Reserve paused raising interest rates, then the market might be more concerned about the economy and earnings. This could result in wider corporate bond spreads and lower stock prices.
The Federal Reserve faces difficult tasks with the employment numbers that have been published , as the economy could be at near full employment. This begs the question could Apple (NASDAQ: AAPL ) find enough workers to produce its products in the US. While listening to CNBC (I think), an analyst mentioned that 1 million workers in China are employed working on Apple products. Mostly likely Apple and its supplier base would be challenged to locate 1 million new workers.
With falling commodity prices; oil, copper, and lumber have fallen, inflation appears to be contained . Also , money supply growth has slowed. See charts.

Bottom line Expect that the Federal Reserve will increase short-term interest rates at the next meeting given comments in prior meeting minutes and public speeches. Then expect a pause for the economic effect of a potential trade and tariff battle and concerns over a possible government funding issue that could result in a partial government shutdown before the Christmas holiday. The decline in stock prices and the negative wealth effect might impact the shopping season more than currently expected.
